reuse.why: Adds two shared helpers (getProtectedCategoryIds, hiddenFilter) and reuses getSheetValue/batchMessages/undoable, but does not build one category-selection function the actions share, and the template parsing ignores goal-template.ts's own reading of goal_def.

duplication.why: The income-or-protected skip condition is repeated in all six actions, the new action copies setZero's v_categories query verbatim, and copyPreviousMonth re-expresses the hidden rule in JS instead of the new hiddenFilter.

placement.why: All logic stays in budget/actions.ts and the new method is registered in budget/app.ts like its siblings, though SQL fragments are string-spliced into each action.

scope.why: Changes stay on the month-wide actions; setZero gains a hidden filter it did not have before, which is in line with step 1 but changes its query shape.

maintainability.why: The 'which categories does a month-wide action fill' rule is spread over a SQL fragment helper, a protected-id set and per-site conditionals, so each future rule must be added in six places.

bypasses_abstraction.where: copyPreviousMonth applies the hidden/includeHiddenCategories rule itself on prevBudget.hidden/group_hidden instead of going through hiddenFilter; every action keeps its own is_income/isTrackingBudget check.

disguised_duplication.where: The hidden rule exists both as the SQL hiddenFilter fragment and as a JS condition in copyPreviousMonth; the skip condition is repeated with reshaped forms (if/return vs continue, isTracking local) across setZero, setLastMonthSpending and the averages.

abstraction_drift.where: hiddenFilter(includeHidden, strictGroup) grows an include flag and a strictGroup special case for the averages' group rule; copyPreviousMonth bypasses it with its own hidden check, and the income/protected checks remain inline at every call site.
